newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures lose ground but seen rallying.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures lose ground but seen rallying.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures lost ground on Tuesday at the start of the second half of Japan's fiscal year but dealers said the market had been oversold and should rebound soon.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract settled 80 points lower at 21,475 points.

"I see this as a technical fall," said one Singapore-based Japanese dealer. "People are worried about the general elections...but I think the short-term bull-trend is intact and anything under 21,500 points is a good buy."
"I would even encourage buying calls at 21,500," he added.
Japan's general election is scheduled for October 20 but there is still little indication of the outcome of the polls.
A survey published on Tuesday showed more voters were uncommitted than supported the most popular contenders, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party.
Another dealer said the Nikkei had fallen back with the slippage of the dollar which briefly dropped back below 111 yen mid-afternoon on Tuesday after hitting a 32-month high of 111.68 yen overnight.
